answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents bind identity to cryptographic attestation chains verified via zero-knowledge proofs. New nodes face progressive collateral staking where minting keys costs $C(n) = k \cdot 2^n$, creating exponential capital exhaustion for any swarm attempting to forge identities. Much like a raven navigating a gale, honest agents traverse verification unscathed, while attacker costs scale superlinearly to absolute bankruptcy.
